messages:
Mike (SRE): FYI getting a bunch of p95/p99 latency alerts from EU clients since ~08:10UTC, support case #12345 attached. Customers report API timeouts and long tail. :warning:
Amanda (Support): +1, multiple tickets call it out as 'very slow in EU -> APAC flows', screenshots show 6-12s latencies on token generation calls. I forwarded logs to ops.
support-bot: New support case #12345 created by Amanda (Support) referencing transaction ids [tx: 0a1b2c].
Maya (Oncall): I see our SLOs are breached on eu-west1 -> apac-edge paths, p99 jumped from 280ms to 1.3s. No errors in app logs, just long TLS handshakes and retries.
Mike (SRE): Repro steps I ran: curl against hosted endpoint with region hint, observed TLS handshake timings large. Sample:
```
$ curl -v --resolve api.redwood.test:443:52.17.23.5 
*   Trying 52.17.23.5:443...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.redwood.test (52.17.23.5) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering h2
* TLS handshake start
* TLS handshake completed in 1.12s
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/2
```
Santiago (Net): Running traceroute from eu-west-pop to apac-pop shows extra cross-AZ hop and a 900ms link at hop 7. Paste: 
```
traceroute to apac-pop (10.200.8.12), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.1.0.1  0.2 ms  0.1 ms  0.2 ms
 2  100.64.23.9  1.1 ms  1.0 ms  1.0 ms
 3  203.0.113.17  5.4 ms  5.2 ms  5.3 ms
 4  198.51.100.45  12.3 ms  12.1 ms  12.2 ms
 5  198.51.100.81  20.2 ms  20.1 ms  20.1 ms
 6  198.51.100.99  35.1 ms  34.9 ms  900.6 ms  <-- flapping / huge delay
 7  10.200.8.12  901.1 ms  899.9 ms  900.3 ms
```
Mike (SRE): That 900ms hop looks like a degraded transit or hairpin. Also noticed higher TLS retry counts (SYN retrans and handshake timeouts) in network logs.
Jiang (Infra): No code deploys in last 6 hours. We did run a BGP policy refresh earlier at 07:50UTC to roll out route preference changes for a subset of prefixes (change id bgp-roll-2026-03). Rolling back would be heavy but possible.
Santiago (Net): Quick checks: DNS resolution for api.redwood.test from EU is returning anycast IP 52.17.23.5 which normally points to eu-pop-A. But AS path shows a fallback via partner transit into apac region for some prefixes. Dig snippet:
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.test @8.8.8.8
52.17.23.5
52.17.23.5
```
Mike (SRE): Mitigation option 1: Force client-side regional pinning for affected customers (support can add header X-Region: eu-west) — quick but not ideal globally.
Amanda (Support): We can ask affected customers to add the header as temporary workaround, but lots will resist. Need platform mitigation.
Maya (Oncall): Mitigation option 2: On edge, increase handshake timeouts and enable aggressive keepalive so existing connections survive. That reduces user impact but raises resource use.
Jiang (Infra): Mitigation option 3: Revert the bgp-roll-2026-03 changes (we can rollback the route-preference change) — that should remove the hairpin and restore normal AS path. Risk: small window of route instability during rollback.
Santiago (Net): I pushed a targeted reroute to avoid partner-transit for the problematic prefix group (manual localpref change) at 08:36UTC for eu-west-pop only — monitoring now.
infra-bot: Route change bgp:apply applied (change-id=manual-eu-avoid-pt-1768) initiated by Santiago.
Mike (SRE): After Santiago's manual reroute p95 dropped back to ~320ms and p99 to ~420ms in 8 minutes. TLS handshake times now ~60-80ms.
Amanda (Support): Sent update to customers w/ advisory and ETA for full rollback. Some customers reported immediate improvement. :thumbsup:
Maya (Oncall): We should still follow up w/ a full postmortem. Action items:
- Jiang: schedule bgp-roll-2026-03 rollback or re-audit the policy (ETA 2h)
- Santiago: collect AS path dumps and partner transit logs (ETA 1h)
- Mike: gather TLS metrics, handshake histograms, and correlate with ticket ids (ETA 45m)
- Amanda: consolidate customer symptom list + affected prefixes (ETA 30m)
Mike (SRE): Quick repro commands I used for capture:
```
# tcpdump to capture failed handshakes
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn|tcp-ack) != 0 and port 443' -w /tmp/tls-handshake.pcap
# mtr to apac edge
mtr -z -r -c 100 10.200.8.12
```
Santiago (Net): I'll also ask partner to check for packet queuing on their interconnects; early signs point to queueing at their border (the 900ms hop showed >300ms variance).
Jiang (Infra): I'll hold the rollback until we confirm partner fix OR schedule a controlled rollback at 10:30UTC (low traffic). Will post in this thread before doing it.
Amanda (Support): Noted. I'll push interim status to open tickets: improvement after reroute, rollback pending.
Mike (SRE): Thanks all. Adding note: consider adding synthetic TLS handshake checks from multiple EU POPs to APAC POPs to catch this earlier. Filing follow-up ticket infra-2345.
Maya (Oncall): Great. Keeping watch here, will page if p99 climbs again.
support-bot: Support case #12345 updated: status -> monitoring.
(ongoing monitoring messages later)
Mike (SRE): 09:02UTC summary: manual reroute stabilized metrics, customers improving, planning postmortem and BGP policy audit. Closing immediate escalation.
